summary: Ten bounded public showcase routes are accepted from current retained evidence. Turbo Drift Circuit and Skyline Runner now pass manual review after replacement-asset rebuilds, corrected camera/contact evidence, and inspected before/after gameplay frames. Two game-layer proof routes remain diagnostics with downward visual vetoes.

routes.subject: Product Configurator public-quality candidate
routes.compositionNotes: The headphones are the clear product hero in a dark product-studio frame, with the title and certified asset card kept outside the evidence area and the configurator controls consolidated into a bottom dock.
routes.notes: Acceptable as a bounded public Aura3D product configurator demo. The route uses the typed headphones GLB, removes the previous debug/proof-wall presentation from the public UI, and keeps material/rendering claims limited to current root evidence.

routes.subject: Material and Asset Inspector public candidate
routes.compositionNotes: The inspected headphones are presented as the clear hero subject on a dark, uncluttered stage. View and lighting controls, material cards, inspection evidence, and the asset passport are contained in a bottom/right dock outside the evidence crop, with no raw JSON wall, text overflow, or clipped diagnostic primitives visible in the public view.
routes.notes: Acceptable as a bounded public Aura3D material/asset inspector demo. The route uses the typed headphones GLB, keeps material claims limited to root-safe material comparison, and treats release/deploy evidence as concise insight rather than the main visual.

routes.subject: Smart City Control public candidate
routes.compositionNotes: The typed city vehicle is the immediate hero subject inside a procedural city-control environment. District and camera controls are grouped in a restrained top command bar, live operations controls sit in the lower-left, and telemetry is contained in a lower-right card outside the vehicle evidence area.
routes.notes: Acceptable as a bounded public Aura3D smart-city/control demo. The route uses the release-validated typed vehicle asset, keeps the procedural city as supporting context, and limits claims to route-local visual operations controls and telemetry evidence.

routes.subject: Architectural District public candidate
routes.compositionNotes: The rejected blockout-style building and gallery primitives are no longer the public composition. The route now frames the typed SkylineCity architecture asset as a readable district model, keeps the whole subject inside the evidence crop, removes the giant contact-shadow blob, and places controls in a restrained right panel outside the asset foreground.
routes.notes: Acceptable as a bounded public Aura3D architecture/district demo. The route proves typed GLB staging, camera choreography, and route evidence while explicitly avoiding HDR, IBL, postprocess, shadow parity, PBR parity, or final architectural visualization fidelity claims.

routes.subject: Digital Twin Operations public candidate
routes.compositionNotes: The rejected OrangeIndustrialRobot composition is no longer the public scene. The route now frames the typed RoboticWeldingWorkcell asset as an enclosed industrial cell with visible safety panels, workcell equipment, HMI details, sensor posts, workpieces, and bounded ops dashboard UI outside the evidence area.
routes.notes: Acceptable as a bounded public Aura3D digital-twin/industrial demo. The route uses a release-validated optimized typed workcell asset, deterministic browser-side telemetry, and restrained support cues while explicitly avoiding real facility integration or production simulation claims.

routes.subject: Blockfall Reactor public candidate
routes.compositionNotes: Current screenshot is playfield-first: the falling-block board is centered, fully framed, and readable; the rejected cabinet, pinball-machine, and controller props are removed from the public composition.
routes.notes: Accepted as a bounded public falling-block demo only if regenerated evidence confirms the prop clutter remains absent and the board/gameplay stays readable.

routes.subject: Public Racing Presentation candidate
routes.compositionNotes: The route now frames a grounded typed sports car on a smoother generated racing loop with a dark integrated start pad, embedded start/finish markings, low side checkpoint markers, and compact HUD. Desktop shows the car plus upcoming road; mobile is pulled back enough to avoid the previous asset-inspection close-up.
routes.notes: Accepted as a bounded public racing presentation route after the July 2 polish pass. The route uses the typed sports car as the visible hero, keeps Tsukuba as manifest-backed topology provenance, and limits claims to root-safe generated racing presentation helpers and route-local gameplay proof.

routes.subject: Public Platformer Presentation candidate
routes.compositionNotes: The route frames a grounded typed walking character on a generated side-scroller stage with readable platforms, subtle trims, red hazards, checkpoint posts, a finish marker, and a compact HUD outside the main evidence area. The typed side-scroller world is retained as playable-surface provenance rather than rendered as the public foreground wall.
routes.notes: Accepted as a bounded public platformer presentation route after the July 3 build. The route uses the typed walking character as the visible hero, keeps SideScrollerWorld as manifest-backed surface-map provenance, and limits claims to root-safe generated platformer presentation helpers and route-local gameplay proof.

routes.subject: Racing Game Layer Proof diagnostic route
routes.compositionNotes: The typed car and circuit are present with retained topology evidence, but the scene reads as a diagnostic harness. Track scale, camera framing, visible proof gates, and overall presentation do not meet public racing showcase quality.
routes.notes: Retain this route as game-layer diagnostic proof only. It proves geometry contracts, certification helpers, retained screenshot-hash plumbing, and keyboard gameplay proof; it does not prove public-quality racing presentation or Turbo/Skyline readiness.

routes.subject: Platformer Game Layer Proof diagnostic route
routes.compositionNotes: The typed character and world are present with retained playable-surface evidence, but the scene reads as a diagnostic harness. The character is not visibly grounded on a platform, debug surface guides are visible, and the composition is not public-quality platformer presentation.
routes.notes: Retain this route as game-layer diagnostic proof only. It proves geometry contracts, certification helpers, retained screenshot-hash plumbing, and keyboard gameplay proof; it does not prove public-quality platformer presentation or Turbo/Skyline readiness.

routes.subject: Skyline Runner public platformer candidate
routes.compositionNotes: The current desktop and mobile frames present a readable grounded character within a cohesive verdant typed platform world. Platforms, hazards, collectibles, checkpoint progression, and finish direction remain visually distinct; responsive framing keeps both the character and traversal path readable without debug surface guides.
routes.notes: Accepted as a bounded public platformer presentation. Manual review inspected the current route-primary image (sha256-95bd1c7e6af04bd64f1fdecd502b28d5233ae85083c7801daf9d74e0731cdc6e), current before/after keyboard frames, and fresh desktop/mobile captures; claims remain limited to certified surface-bound presentation and public genre-kit gameplay proof.

routes.subject: Turbo Drift Circuit public racing candidate
routes.compositionNotes: The current desktop and mobile frames present a readable player car plus a smaller deterministic ghost on a cohesive typed neon circuit, with upcoming road remaining legible from the evidence-selected camera. The compact HUD and controls stay outside the primary car/road contact area, and input evidence shows clear motion without debug guides.
routes.notes: Accepted as a bounded public racing presentation. Manual review inspected the current route-primary image (sha256-59a678f67d6eeb4d4a1cdb911e9002516e099ecdbb7512da795ec2c53587d9a3), current before/after keyboard frames, and fresh desktop/mobile captures. The second vehicle is a deterministic route-progress ghost, not AI; claims remain limited to certified topology-bound presentation and public genre-kit gameplay proof.
